hero.traceAria: Profile of one Nordschleife lap: flat out on the straights, dips in the corners
hero.traceCaption: One lap of the Nordschleife, read from the track's corner radii. Up is flat out, down is a corner.
hero.lede: I'm doing my Ausbildung as a Fachinformatiker für Anwendungsentwicklung at Herrenknecht AG. Backend at work, frontend and fullstack for fun.

about.title: The person behind the code.
about.text: Heyy, I'm Kevin, 19 years old. Day to day I work in the backend team at Herrenknecht AG, which I can't really show off here. So on my own time I mostly build fullstack and frontend stuff for fun, like this site.
about.offText: Outside of work I'm usually deep in sim racing and motorsport, working through a rotating cast of games, or catching up on an anime.
about.offAction: See what I'm into off duty

builds.title: Things I've built.
builds.text: My work projects are under NDA, so everything here happened in my own time.

items.lunasOs: My personal dashboard for everyday life and vocational school: todos, calendar, timetable, grades and notes straight from my Obsidian vault.
items.lunaracing: Telemetry tracker for Le Mans Ultimate. It stores every lap, draws the track from position data and puts laps side by side.
items.lunair: Invite-only photo feed for my friends, with posts, comments, reactions and a shared virtual pet that wants to be fed.
items.lunagraph: Knowledge graph for Next.js and TypeScript codebases, so Claude Code can look things up instead of re-reading the whole project. The goal is an MCP server.
items.discordBot: Server management bot with tickets, audit log, welcome messages, moderation tools and mini games. Recently rebuilt from scratch in Python.
items.portfolio: The page you're on. Next.js, TypeScript and CSS Modules, with a few easter eggs hidden in it.
items.karteikarten: Flashcard app for building and studying decks, with saved progress and login. Started as a team project during my time at DHBW.
items.pygame: A Mario-style platformer to get back into Pygame and sharpen my Python. Going open source later.

path.title: The lap so far.
path.text: Laid out on my favorite circuit, the Nürburgring Nordschleife. Each checkpoint is a corner on the lap, in the real order you'd drive them.
path.mapAria: Map of the Nürburgring Nordschleife with 7 checkpoints marking my career timeline
path.caption: Nordschleife, 20.8 km, real track geometry. Tap a checkpoint.

1.title: Interested in IT
1.text: I was in 9th grade when I first got interested in IT. I did internships at local companies to get a feel for the industry.

2.title: Tech. Highschool
2.text: A tech-focused school, where I got in touch with programming and a lot of different technologies.

3.title: Side projects
3.text: I built a Discord bot and small Python scripts to apply what I learned and get a better understanding of programming.

4.title: Herrenknecht AG
4.text: I applied as a dual student in IT, got accepted and started working there in July 2025.

5.title: Dual student
5.text: Alongside the work at Herrenknecht I studied at DHBW Karlsruhe, split between practical work and coursework.

6.title: Changing direction
6.text: I left the dual-study program. Lectures plus full-time work wasn't the right fit, so I looked for a path that's more hands-on.

7.title: Ausbildung
7.text: Since 1 September 2026: a full apprenticeship as Fachinformatiker für Anwendungsentwicklung at Herrenknecht AG, full-time and hands-on through 2028.

offDuty.text: Lately I've been really into sim racing and motorsport in general. I love the realism and the competition that comes with it. Outside that, I play a variety of games to unwind.

privacy.title: Data protection
privacy.intro: Most of this site does not use analytics, tracking, or cookies, and does not collect any personal data. The Pit Wall guestbook is the exception. Here is what it collects and why:
privacy.messagesText: Anything you post to the Pit Wall (your display name and message, plus your Discord name and avatar if you sign in) is stored and shown publicly on that page.
privacy.discordBefore: Signing in with Discord is handled by Discord's own OAuth login. This site receives your Discord user ID, display name, and avatar URL, which are stored so your entry can show up as a Discord post. See
privacy.discordAfter: for how Discord itself handles your data.
privacy.spamBefore: Submitting to the Pit Wall runs a Cloudflare Turnstile check, which processes some technical signals about your browser/request to tell humans from bots. See
privacy.spamAfter: . A salted, one-way hash of your IP address is also stored for up to 24 hours to rate-limit repeated submissions; the hash cannot be reversed back into an IP address, and it is not linked to your message.
privacy.removal: Want a guestbook entry removed? Get in touch using the contact details above.

startLights.title: How fast are you off the line?
startLights.text: Five reds, a random hold, then green. Your time is from green to your click. Go early and it's a jump start.

pad.idleSub: then hit it again the moment the lights turn green
pad.jumpEarly: You went before green. Press again to retry.
pad.jumpAnticipated: Under {min} ms is guessing, not reacting. Press again to retry.
pad.unranked: Leaderboard unreachable, just for fun. Press again for another go
